ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early‑Dead set packed with rare blues and fledgling originals
ai_show_review.blurb: The Matrix show delivers raw psychedelic R&B grit with standout cuts like Me And My Uncle, Early Morning Rain and a Pigpen‑led Big Boy Pete. Jerry’s guitar stays solid despite a cold, while Bill Kreutzmann opens the set with a bebop‑style drum figure. The performance feels like a curated showcase of early rarities.
ai_show_review.review: November 29, 1966 at The Matrix captures the Grateful Dead in a feverish, raw phase that still crackles after six decades. From the opening “Me And My Uncle” through a string of deep‑cut numbers—“The Same Thing,” “Stealin’,” “Big Boy Pete,” and “Early Morning Rain”—the band rides a high‑energy current of psychedelic R&B. Pigpen’s commanding presence on “Big Boy Pete” spurs a playful vocal trade with Jerry, while Bill Kreutzmann’s bebop‑style drum intro sets an inventive tone for the night. Despite battling a cold, Garcia’s guitar work remains tight and melodic, especially on “Cold Rain And Snow,” and Phil steps up to handle vocals on several tunes, adding a different texture to the set. The third set continues the deep‑cut theme with “Down So Long,” “There's Something On Your Mind,” and “I Just Want To Make Love To You,” cementing this show as a rare snapshot of the Dead’s early repertoire performed at full tilt.

best_recording.reason: Despite lo‑fi hiss, this soundboard captures the full set’s raw energy and includes all the standout early‑Dead rarities in a single, complete source.
